newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India's August Bombay High crude production down.
newsitem.headline: India's August Bombay High crude production down.

text.p: Crude oil production at India's state Oil and Natural Gas Corp Ltd's offshore Bombay High Basin fell by 11 percent year-on-year in August, an ONGC spokesman said on Monday.

The spokesman said crude oil production from India's largest hydrocarbon producing area, the Bombay High Basin, fell to 1.784 million tonnes in August this year, compared to 1.994 million tonnes last year.
He said although production rose from July's 1.69 million tonnes, the increase was marginal and "nothing unusual."
"It is not a drastic improvement," the spokesman said.
However, he said an incremental rise in output was expected in March or April next year from the Neelam Field.
ONGC is studying ways to boost production at Neelam, one of three major fields at the Basin, which has been falling since its commissioning in 1994.

The failing Neelam field is expected to bring down the Basin's total output to 18.5 million tonnes in this fiscal year (March-April), from 21.4 million tonnes produced in the last fiscal year, he said.
Gas production from the Basin in August rose year-on-year to 1,171.2 million cubic metres from 1,130.7 million cubic metres.
But the Basin's liquid petroleum gas (LPG) output in August fell to 93,111 tonnes from 93,221 tonnes year-on-year.
